melanoma_advanced.label: Ongoing treatment and review
melanoma_advanced.prescription_note: No routine prophylactic antiemetic or premedication is specified for this monotherapy. Any symptom-treatment medicine requires an individual authorised prescription.
additional_support: Immunotherapy can cause inflammation in healthy organs during treatment or after it stops. Contact the oncology team promptly for new diarrhoea, blood in stools, cough or breathlessness, yellow skin or eyes, severe headache, vision changes, marked thirst, unusual weakness or a spreading rash. Tell any clinician that you are receiving or have received immunotherapy.

Discuss fertility before starting. Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. Tell the team promptly about a possible pregnancy. Discuss breastfeeding restrictions with the team before treatment; do not breastfeed without their advice. Do not stop prescribed steroids or hormone replacement yourself.
Immune adverse effects may require corticosteroids and/or long-term hormone replacement under specialist direction. Do not stop prescribed treatment yourself.
This is an incomplete clinical/pharmacy review draft, not an issued prescription.
